newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds rise sharply.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds rose sharply on Monday on expectations of easing inflation and interest rates, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.14 pct to 103.04
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 102.06
Volume was low at 120 million shekels.
"Turnover was very low today. Investors are focusing on the stock market, which is rising sharply. Bonds are becoming less attractive," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI).
Inflation-linked bonds fell on profit-taking, but he said the decline would not continue.
"I'm sure that tomorrow they'll recover again. The Bank of Israel has stopped issuing new long bonds and yields will continue to decline (from 4.1 percent) to less than four percent," he said.
"Investors were focusing today on unlinked bonds because the market expects a moderate rate cut following the lower than-expected-consumer price index," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
The January consumer price index, which was published on Friday, rose 0.4 percent, compared with an 0.8 percent increase in December. The January index was slightly under estimates.
"The central bank might leave its key base rate unchanged, but it is clear that in the long run interest rates will continue to decline," the FIBI trader said.
Makams also rose on hopes for a rate cut but activity was low, the Leumi trader added.

Dollar-linked bonds closed sharply higher, which traders said followed the rise of the U.S. currency in Europe. In the local forex market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3510 shekels against 3.3410 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
